formula: Subject + have got / has got + object   |   my / your / his / her / our / their + noun
when_to_use: Use possessive adjectives to show who something belongs to, and have got / has got to talk about family and belongings.
when_to_use_ar: نستخدم صفات الملكية لبيان مين صاحب الشيء، و have got / has got للكلام عن العائلة والممتلكات.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic attaches possession as a suffix (كتابي = 'book-my'), so the separate word order 'my book' feels reversed. Also Arabic uses 'عندي' (at me) rather than a 'have' verb.

examples.en: I have got a small family.

common_errors.explanation: The possessive comes BEFORE the noun in English.

common_errors.wrong: I have got a brother his name Ali.
common_errors.correct: I have got a brother. His name is Ali.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: ___ house is near the school (of them).

quick_rule: Possessive BEFORE the noun. I/you/we/they → have got · he/she/it → has got.
quick_rule_ar: صفة الملكية قبل الاسم. و has got مع he/she/it فقط.
connect_to_speaking: Describe your family: 'I have got two sisters. My father is a teacher. Their names are ___.'
